bug_report_content:
id: 378
status: Fixed
summary: Overzealous arguments optimisation
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 2
commentCount: 15
Comment 0 (2011-03-12): Consider the following JavaScript code: function d3_call(callback) { var f = callback; arguments[0] = this; f.apply(this, arguments); return this; } This is optimised to: function d3_call(a){arguments[0]=this;a.apply(this,arguments);return this}; However, the use of a temporary variable `f` is necessary to avoid `arguments[0] = this` from overwriting the first argument. In the above optimised code, `arguments[0] = this` causes `this` to be assigned to `a`. Verified on latest SVN r878. See also: https://github.com/mbostock/d3/issues/closed#issue/68
Comment 1 (2011-03-14): Good find! The both variable inliner should not be inlining across an arguments access like this.
Comment 3 (2011-03-14): Forgot to mention, I will be looking at this in a bit. Thanks.
Comment 4 (2011-03-16): FYI: I put in a fix. Currently pending review.
Comment 5 (2011-03-24): r911 and r896
Comment 6 (2011-03-24): Doesn't appear to work; tested the latest release 20110322 on the code above and the same thing happens.
Comment 7 (2011-03-24): Reopen, still an issue.
Comment 8 (2011-03-28): This issue was closed by revision r942.
Comment 9 (2011-03-28): Still not working I'm afraid, the output as of r942 is: function d3_call(a){var b;arguments[0]=this;a.apply(this,arguments);return this}; Notice how nothing is assigned to b and "a.apply" is used.
Comment 10 (2011-03-28): Reopen.
Comment 11 (2011-03-28): it would be nice if there were real integration tests for this issue, rather than just unit tests.
Comment 12 (2011-03-30): Should be fixed with r949. Care to verify.
Comment 13 (2011-03-31): Perfect, thanks!
